question: What should you do if you want to turn right at an intersection controlled by a red arrow light?
options: Come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and cross traffic, and then turn right
Wait until the light changes to green before making your turn
Slow down and turn right if no vehicles are approaching
Honk briefly to alert pedestrians and turn right
explanation: You may not turn right if you are stopped at a red arrow light; you must wait until the light changes to green.

question: While waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, how should you position your front wheels?
options: Pointed to the left so you can turn quickly when traffic clears
Pointed to the right toward the curb
Pointed straight ahead until it is safe to start your turn
Turned slightly left with your foot off the brake
explanation: Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead while waiting to turn left so that if you are hit from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: Under what condition are you allowed to make a left turn against a red light?
options: When turning from a two-way street onto a one-way street
When turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street, unless a sign prohibits the turn
When turning into a private driveway after midnight
Never; left turns on red are always illegal in California
explanation: You may turn left against a red light only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street and no sign prohibits the turn.

question: When is it legal to make a U-turn in a residential district?
options: Whenever you use a fire station driveway to turn around
When no vehicles are approaching you within 200 feet
Only at intersections with a traffic signal
Whenever you cannot see clearly for 100 feet in each direction
explanation: You may make a U-turn in a residential district if no vehicles are approaching you within 200 feet.

question: In a business district, where are you permitted to make a U-turn?
options: Anywhere across a single set of double yellow lines
In front of a fire station if no emergency vehicles are present
Only at an intersection or on a divided highway where an opening is provided, unless a NO U-TURN sign is posted
Anywhere as long as no vehicles are within 100 feet
explanation: In business districts, U-turns are prohibited except at an intersection or on a divided highway where an opening has been provided.

question: How long before exiting a freeway should you signal your intention to exit?
options: At least 2 seconds (approximately 100 feet) before exiting
At least 3 seconds (approximately 200 feet) before exiting
At least 5 seconds (approximately 400 feet) before exiting
Only after your vehicle enters the deceleration lane
explanation: When in the proper lane to exit a freeway, you should signal five seconds (approximately 400 feet) before you exit.

question: How much space do you need to safely merge, enter, or exit traffic on a city street versus on a highway?
options: A quarter block (75 feet) on city streets; half a block (150 feet) on the highway
Half a block (about 150 feet) on city streets; a full block (about 300 feet) on the highway
One full block on both city streets and highways
100 feet on city streets; 200 feet on the highway
explanation: To safely merge, enter, or exit traffic, you need half a block (about 150 feet) on city streets and a full block (about 300 feet) on the highway.

question: Within what distance of an intersection, bridge, tunnel, or railroad crossing is passing another vehicle prohibited?
options: Within 50 feet
Within 100 feet
Within 200 feet
Within 300 feet
explanation: You must not pass within 100 feet of an intersection, bridge, tunnel, railroad crossing, or other hazardous area.
